messages:
alex kim: Heads-up — Riverbank asked for a POC but their API produces consistent output drift. Looks like tokenization and stop-seq handling differ. Can we map token deltas and propose a mitigation for stop sequences? Also: they asked for a pricing example if token counts increase by ~20%.

mira patel: We ran a quick diff on a 3k-char prompt set — average token delta ~8%, worst-case 22% when emojis + zero-width joiners present. Stop sequences sometimes split across tokens so the model doesn't truncate as expected.

ethan (se): Re: tokenization — normalization helps. Recommend NFC and trimming repeated whitespace before tokenizing. Send a zipped sample of their top 100 prompts and I can produce a token-delta report. For stop seqs we can post-process generated stream and enforce sequence detection on decoded text, then cut off.

sam (infra): Note an infra wrinkle: their adapter pads messages differently which changes KV cache alignment and latency. For the POC we'll run with batch_size=1 and disable long-prefetch to avoid tail latency spikes. Can toggle for later benchmarks.

natalie (pm): Customer wants a clear cost comparison: show 3 scenarios (baseline, +8% tokens, +20% tokens) with monthly usage 1M chats, avg 600 tokens per chat. We'll include hosted vs Dedicated estimates. Alex, can you draft the pricing slide?

alex kim: Yep. Ethan — can you provide sample script/snippets we can hand to their infra for local validation? Also they asked about streaming billing — do we show partial token charging details?

ethan (se): I'll drop a small script in the repo. Example snippet: ```python
# quick tokenizer diff
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
tok = Tokenizer.from_file('redwood-tokenizer.json')
s = open('sample.txt','rb').read().decode('utf-8')
print(len(tok.encode(s).ids))
```
For billing: we bill per-request tokens (prompt + response). Streaming increments are reconciled post-hoc; the invoice will reflect full consumed tokens. I'll add example math for the slide.

mira patel: Security Q: they sent an infosec questionnaire asking whether we forward raw client IPs and store downstream headers. Private deployments can turn off X-Forwarded-For; hosted requires minimal logging. @sam (infra) is toggling header forwarding for the POC safe?

sam (infra): No blocker. We can disable X-Forwarded-For and enable request header redaction in the proxy. For audit we can enable KMS-wrapped access logs with redaction rules. Legal will need the retention SLA sign-off.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment 0.12.3 -> staging started by @sam (infra) at 2025-10-01T14:12Z

ethan (se): For parity testing I recommend an A/B harness: same prompts, fixed seed, temperature 0, compare top-k overlap and token output diffs. I'll run 2k prompts and produce a diff CSV and sample response pairs for review.

natalie (pm): Good plan. Request: schedule a 30m sync with Riverbank Wed week after next. Alex, please upload the sample prompts + token-diff report by EOD Monday so we can share ahead of the call.

alex kim: Will do — uploading samples and the slide deck link in this thread shortly. Adding cost scenarios and the script from @ethan (se). :thumbsup:
